full_judgment:
SM Ziaul Karim J : This Rule was issued, on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, at the instance of accused petitioner, calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 27-9-2006 passed by the Metropolitan Session Judge, Chittagong, rejecting Criminal Revision No. 299 of 2005 and confirming the order dated 28-8-2005 passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, in CR Case No. 2969 of 2004, rejecting an application of accused under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, should not be quashed or to pass such order or orders as the Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Pending hearing of the Rule the proceeding of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 was stayed for period of 1 (one) year. Subsequently the stay order was extended from time to time. 

 5. Short facts leading to this Rule are that the complainant opposite party No. 2 filed CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong on 16-9-2004 accusing three accused namely 1 Md Faridul. Islam, 2 SM Abbas Uddin and 3. Mohammad Hanif alleging, inter alia, to the effect that complainant Md Mahabubur Rahman took loan of Tk 5 lac and Taka 2 laces on 1-12-2001 and 18-2-2002 respectively from accused Faridul Islam on condition to make repayment of the said loan amount afterwards and as security complainant handed over to accused Faridul Islam two blank signed non-Judicial Stamps one of Taka 100 and other of Taka 50 and one blank signed cartridge paper. It was agreed upon between the parties that above accused Faridul Islam would return those two blank signed non-Judicial Stamps and one blank signed cartridge paper when this loan amount as above be paid back by the complainant who afterwards on 20-3-2003 wanted to make payment of said loan amount and to take back those two blank signed non-Judicial Stamps and blank signed cartridge paper, but accused Faridul Islam refused to accept the repayment of above loan amount and also refused to return above two blank signed non-Judicial Stamps and blank signed cartridge paper to the complainant. Complainant further alleged that accused in collusion with each other created and fabricated false bainapatra for property belonged to him on aforesaid two blank signed non-Judicial stamps and on one blank signed cartridge paper handed over to the accused Faridul Islam as security of the said loan amount. Accordingly, CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 was filed against above three accused under sections 467/468 /471/474/34 of the Penal Code before Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. The matter was sent for judicial enquiry and report. After receipt of the report cognisance under sections 468, 34 of the Penal Code was taken against all three accused by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. Mean-while, the accused appeared in the case and were bailed out. 

 6. On date fixed for framing charge a petition under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was filed by accused for postponement or stay of the proceeding of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 till disposal of OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 filed on 5-11-2002 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong, by accused Faridul Islam against complaint Mahbubur Rahman for Specific Performance of Contract based on aforesaid bainapatra dated 10-4-2001. Complainant raised objection and upon hearing both sides the application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was rejected by Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong by its order 28-8-2005 and charge under sections 468, 34 of the Penal Code was framed against three accused. 

 8. Feeling aggrieved one of three accused namely Md Hanif as petitioner preferred application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before this Court and obtained Rule as above in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2039 of 2007. 

 10. Mr JBM Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused petitioner, supports the Rule and refers to his supplementary affidavit dated 17-3-2008 showing the certified copy of Firisti, by which document including original Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 were filed and produced in OC. Suit No. 110 of 2002 filed in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong, by accused Faridul Islam as plaintiff against complainant of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 as defendant for Specific Performance of Contract. He adds that when the original Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 (subject matter of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004) was already produced by Firisti in OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 for Specific Performance of Contract based on same Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong, said Civil Court will be competent to file complaint about forgery of the Bainapatra produced during trial of the Civil Suit and any private complaint in such regard will be barred under section 195(C) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He accordingly argues that when same Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 is the subject of scrutiny by above Civil Court in OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 filed long before filing of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 for forgery of the said Bainapatra, the CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 should be kept stayed or postponed till disposal of OC Suit No. 110 of 2002, now pending in the first Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong. Showing above facts and circumstances as well as law point as above learned Advocate earnestly submits that learned Metropolitan Session Judge, Chittagong did not properly appreciate the above law point as involved as well as circumstances and quite erroneously rejected Criminal Revision No. 299 of 2005 by its impugned judgment and order dated 27-9-2006 illegally upholding the order dated 28-8-2005 by Metropolitan Magistrate rejecting the prayer under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the accused of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004. 

 12. Mr Helaluddin, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, for the State opposite party No. 1, supports the contention of learned Advocate for the accused petitioner stating that when same Bainapatra which is alleged by complainant of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 to be forged and fabricated, is also a subject of scrutiny in OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 filed by accused Faridul Islam as plaintiff against complainant Mahabubur Rahman as defendant for Specific Performance of Contract based on such Bainapatra and, as such, the CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 is required to be stayed at least for limited period facilitating for disposal and decision about said Bainapatra in above Civil Suit. He adds that if during trial of Civil Suit the Court finds the said Bainapatra to be creation of forgery the Court itself can file complaint before Criminal Court and private complaint about said Bainapatra will be barred under section 195(C) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Learned Assistant Attorney-General therefore, raises no serious objection to the Rule. 

 13. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the complainant opposite party No. 2, opposes the Rule and submits that present petitioner Md Hanif being not a party to the Civil Suit (OC Suit No. 110 of 2002) before Civil Court, can have no locus standi to file the present Miscellaneous Case No. 2039 of 2007 under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the relief as prayed for. He next submits that the present application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is, in fact, a second revision under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which is untenable in law, inasmuch as the petitioner did not state anything new in the application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure except what were agitated in Criminal Revision Case No. 299 of 2005 under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before Metropolitan Session Judge, Chittagong. 

 15. We have considered the contentions of all sides as above, we have perused the application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the copy of plaint of OC Suit No. 110 of 2002, copy of petition of complaint of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004, we have also perused the certified copy of the Firisti furnished with the supplementary affidavit in this Miscellaneous Case as to filing of the Original of Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 in OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 for Specific Performance of Contract pending in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong by Faridul Islam as plaintiff against complainant opposite party No. 2 Mahabubur Rahman as defendant in the said OC Suit. 

 16. On perusal it appears that OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 was filed by one Faridul Islam as plaintiff against Mahbubur Rahman as defendant for Specific Performance of Contract based on Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 executed by said Mahabubur Rahman relating to land belonging to him upon Contract for sale to the plaintiff Faridul Islam who was made accused No. 1 in CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 under sections 467, 468, 471, 474.34 of Penal Code. Said Faridul Islam is accused No. 1 in CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 filed by Mahabubur Rahman who made a specific allegation in said CR Case that all three accused in collusion with each other created false bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 using two blank and signed non-Judicial Stamps of Taka 100 and Taka 50 and also using the blank and signed Cartridge Paper. Md Hanif was made an accused in above CR Case alleging for creation of false Bainapatra which is subject matter of scrutiny in OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 for Specific Performance of Contract between Faridul Islam and Mahabubur Rahman. The petition under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was filed by all three accused including Faridul Islam and all three accused as petitioners also filed Criminal Revision No. 299 of 2005 before Metropolitan Session Judge, Chittagong. After rejection of said Criminal Revision, Md Hanif as accused petitioner alone preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2039 of 2007 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before this Division. In above context Md Hanif as one of the accused in CR Case for creation of Bainapatra can have locus standi to prefer this application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure to get the CR Case stayed or postponed till disposal of the OC Suit No. 110 of 2002, pending in Civil Court as same bainapatra is the subject of scrutiny in the said Civil Suit also. 

 17. Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2039 of 2007 under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be said to be second revision in the garb of application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the High Court Division. inasmuch as after being unsuccessful in Criminal Revision No. 299 of 2005, the next remedy for the accused petitioners is to seek relief under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the High Court Division. There has not been any procedural and legal error for Md Hanif being one of the accused of CR Case to file application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before High Court Division seeking appropriate relief. Objection as raised by learned Advocate for complainant opposite, party cannot be upheld. 

 18. It is obvious that OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 was filed by Faridul Islam as plaintiff against Mahabubur Rahman as defendant for Specific Performance of Contract based on the Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001. CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 was filed by complainant Mahabubur Rahman against accused No. 1 Faridul Islam and 2 others long after filing of OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 for Specific Performance of Contract alleging to have created false Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 in collusion with other accused including Md Hanif Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 is the subject of scrutiny in both CR Case and OC Suit No. 110 of 2002. 

 20. OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 was filed earlier than CR Case No. 2969 of 2004. Original Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 was already filed in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong in OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 and said Bainapatra was kept in safe custody of the Court as stated earlier. 

 25. In the light of discussion made above this Court feels that in view of the Provisions of section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as above, it appears to the necessary that the trial of the CR Case No 2969 of 2004, now pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong be postponed for a limited period facilitating the disposal of the OC Suit No. 110 of 2002 as to Specific Performance of Contract based on Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 between Faridul Islam and Mahabubur Rahman. 

 26. In such regard reliance may be put on the decision in the case of Abdur Rab Meah vs State reported in 3 BCR 265 wherein it has been held: 

 "In the interest of justice where stay of criminal procedure is expedient and desirable in view of the pendency of a dispute between the parties in the Civil Court on the same subject matter, the Criminal Court may adjourn the criminal case till disposal of the Civil Suit." 

 This view receives support in the case of Zakir Hussain vs State, reported in 43 DLR (AD) 10=1992 BLD (AD) 287. 

 27. In view of the discussions made above and the preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities referred to above we hold that for the ends of justice the criminal case bearing CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 should be stayed for a limited period. Therefore, we are unable to accept the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the opposite party No. 2, on the contrary the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioner prevails and appears to have a good deal of force. 

 28. In the result the Rule is made absolute. The impugned Judgment and order dated 27-9-2006 passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong, rejecting Criminal Revision No. 299 of 2005 and upholding order dated 28-8-2005 passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong rejecting application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as to stay of the proceeding of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 till disposal of OC Suit No. 110 of 2002, pending in First Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong be accordingly quashed. Prayer under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure be allowed in a modified manner as below: 

 29. Proceeding of CR Case No. 2969 of 2004 under sections 468, 34 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong be postponed or stayed for a period of 1(one) year from the date of receipt of this judgment by the Court below. Meanwhile, both sides be directed to move jointly or separately in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong, to arrange for early hearing and disposal of OC. Suit No. 110 of 2002 for Specific Performance of Contract based on Bainapatra dated 10-4-2001 preferably within a period of one year as above.
